title: Building a Store Training System on a Franchise ERP
description: Move store training off paper and spreadsheets: how FDAM links training schedules, scores, and comments to store data so supervisors can coach each owner.
html:
How to turn store training into data with a franchise ERP and connect it to supervisor coaching

store training, franchise ERP, FDAM, HQ training management, supervisor, QSCV, brand standardization, store management, store-opening management, HQ operations system

Key takeaways

· Store training isn't a one-off event; it's where a brand's operating quality begins.

· Paper scorecards and spreadsheet-based training management create breaks in evaluation data and gaps in handovers.

· Training data must accumulate in the ERP for supervisors' store-visit coaching to be tailored.

· FDAM automatically links training schedules, evaluations, and comments to store master data.

A store training system is the HQ infrastructure that makes the operating manuals headquarters gives store owners work consistently in the field. As the store count grows, it gets harder for supervisors to manage every store closely, so the data built up during pre-opening training determines the quality of coaching once stores are operating.

Yet one of the biggest dilemmas for HQ operations teams is the gap between the manual and the field. If training HQ carefully prepared isn't applied consistently in stores, the brand's overall operating quality (QSC) starts to splinter into store-by-store variation. Even so, many HQs still manage training data with spreadsheets and handwritten scorecards. Let's walk through how FDAM, built by MS Venter after nearly 25 years focused on franchise IT, has moved this flow into a system.

Store training remains an HQ asset only when it accumulates in the ERP.

1. Three risks of managing store training without an ERP

Training records that aren't digitized lead to management gaps once stores are operating.

Quite a few HQ staff think, "Training is the training team's job; operations only manages stores after opening." This break in data may not look like a big problem in the short term, but over the long term it drives up HQ management costs quickly.

No objective evaluation data

Paper scorecards don't become data. You can't compare store owners' skills item by item or analyze them as trends, and as a result, it's hard for supervisors to judge what to prioritize in coaching when they visit a store.

Lost history and difficult handovers

When staff leave or change roles, there's no way to find out what training a store owner received before opening or where they fell short. When HQ loses the operating history for an owner, the operations team has to start the same work over from scratch.

Inefficiency from duplicated work

Supervisors responsible for store openings and supervisors responsible for operations end up training or checking the same things twice. Information that an ERP would share with a single entry is stuck inside spreadsheet files.

2. A data-driven training process with FDAM

Training cohorts and trainees link instantly to store master data.

MS Venter's FDAM goes beyond franchise sales management to cover the entire store lifecycle, from training to opening to operations, in a single system. Built on experience working with about 500 brands, it's designed so data from the training stage flows seamlessly into the operations stage.

Step 1. Systematize training schedules and trainees

  • Data integration: Create a cohort in the system instead of by phone or KakaoTalk, and it links instantly to store master data.
  • Documented evidence: At contract renewal or if a dispute arises, you can instantly confirm from system records "when, and which curriculum, was completed."

Step 2. Digital scorecards and automatic scoring

Evaluators check evaluation items (theory, hands-on practice, service mindset, etc.) on a tablet or smartphone on site. The system automatically calculates the total score based on weighting, reducing human error, and results are saved to the cloud in real time so everyone at HQ sees the same screen from anywhere.

3. Training data becomes core material for supervising

Data from the training stage becomes material for supervisors' tailored coaching.

FDAM's real value shows up after training ends, in the work of the operations team and supervisors. Scores and comments accumulated during training flow naturally into the operations management module, so supervisors can understand the owner's context before visiting the store.

"Excellent at learning recipes, but tends to get flustered when handling customer complaints."

When a trainer's comment like this reaches the assigned supervisor through the system, the supervisor can focus on coaching customer service skills rather than menu training on the first store visit. This is how data-driven, tailored supervising takes shape.

Ask the FDAM AI assistant, the first integrated into a Korean franchise ERP, "Show me the stores with the lowest training scores this month," and you'll get a list sorted by score along with priorities for each supervisor. The training data HQ has accumulated is turned into material you can use right away for decisions.

4. Adopting a system creates the brand standard

Store training isn't a one-off event. It's the first promise between HQ and its stores and the point where a brand's operating quality begins. When data accumulated during training flows naturally into operations, inspections, and CS responses, HQ has the foundation to maintain the same quality of operations even as stores multiply.

If you're stacking training scorecards in binders, start by considering how to turn that pile of paper into living data. Once the flow takes hold, it begins to accumulate as an HQ asset from then on.

Frequently asked questions

Q. What's the biggest problem with managing training in spreadsheets without an ERP?

The biggest problems are that individual store owners' evaluation results don't accumulate as statistics, history breaks when staff change, and multiple supervisors inefficiently check the same things. In the end, the HQ operations team keeps having to get to know each store from scratch.

Q. How are training records linked to store master data?

In FDAM, prospective franchisee information registered during franchise sales management carries over into training cohort assignments, and training evaluation results accumulate in the same store owner's master data. After opening, supervisors can see that flow on one screen in operations management, too.

Q. How can supervisors use training data?

Before a store visit, supervisors can check scores and comments accumulated during training and prioritize coaching in the areas where each owner fell short. They can also ask the AI assistant in plain language for a list of stores by score to set visit priorities quickly.

Q. Can training history serve as evidence in a dispute at contract renewal?

Training completion dates, curricula, and evaluation results recorded in the system can serve as objective evidence of the operating support HQ provided to a store owner. They become important evidence at the renewal stage or if a dispute arises.
